key_insight: Water vapor retards grain growth and sintering in yttria-stabilized zirconia, potentially through OH-mediated grain-boundary stabilization.
engineering_relevance: Accounting for steam exposure could improve predictions of porosity retention and thermal-insulation performance in YSZ thermal barrier coatings.
method: Heat-treated YSZ pellets with three initial porosities and free-standing plasma-sprayed coatings at 1300 °C in dry air, steam, or dry nitrogen.
Compared grain growth, porosity, and coating thermal conductivity.
Used DFT and defect-equilibrium sensitivity analysis to investigate OH binding and oxygen-vacancy changes.
evidence_signal: After 100 h, the most porous pellet had 31% smaller grains in steam, with apparent grain-growth rate constants reduced by factors of 2.8–4.2; coatings retained higher porosity and lower thermal conductivity at intermediate exposures.
watch_item: The mechanism is supported by calculations, but performance under service conditions beyond the tested 1300 °C exposures remains unestablished.
paper_title: Water vapor retards grain growth during sintering of yttria-stabilized zirconia pellets and coatings
